mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate tighter policy, causing a short-term discounting effect that depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening episodes are not statistically lower than in pre-tightening episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or FEDFUNDS rise is ≤0.25pp in all observed windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index for three consecutive months signals disinflation, prompting central banks to hold rates steady and reducing risk premia, which results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, forward returns are not statistically different from a baseline of neutral inflation (t-test p > 0.05); or CPIAUCSL does not show three consecutive months of decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 50,000 jobs in the prior month is associated with stronger consumer demand and corporate optimism, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following strong employment gains, forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05); or PAYEMS does not exceed 50,000 in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) shows a double-digit monthly increase, it indicates robust manufacturing momentum that translates into higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >10% in the prior month
failure_condition: In 5-day windows after large positive INDPRO moves, forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05); or INDPRO does not exceed +10% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 5% over two months suggests softening consumer demand, which compresses earnings growth forecasts and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by ≥5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following double-month RSAFS declines of ≥5%, forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05); or RSAFS decline is <5% in any two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for the first time in three months, it signals a strengthening labor market that supports optimism about economic growth and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and declined for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day windows following such UNRATE lows, forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05); or UNRATE does not fall below 4.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both HOUST (housing starts) and GDPC1 (personal consumption) by at least 10% in the prior month indicate dual softening in credit and demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥10% AND GDPC1 falls by ≥10% in the prior month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after such dual declines, forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05); or either proxy does not fall by ≥10% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (as signaled by a 4-month moving average of FEDFUNDS below 1.00%), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be positive over the next 60 trading days due to reduced borrowing costs and risk aversion reduction.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizons in easing regimes, forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05); or 4-month MA(FEDFUNDS) ≥ 1.00% in all observed windows.
